name: azure-openai-deployment-escaping
purpose: AZURE_OPENAI source, DEPLOYMENT NAME ESCAPING: the pinned path is built by interpolating the deployment name RAW into `/openai/deployments/${azure_deployment_name}/chat/completions` and then parsing it with `new URL`, which percent-encodes what the WHATWG path set escapes. A name carrying a space must therefore reach the provider as %20. Without such an input the escaping assertion in this branch would be decoration, because an ASCII-clean name encodes identically whether the name is escaped or not.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: the recording peer's origin is supplied in the request body (azure_base_url = http://<mock>/v1/), so only the PATH and QUERY are the compared contract -- and the /v1/ segment proves the base's own path is DISCARDED by the leading-slash resolution
tier2.reason: AZURE_OPENAI has NO pinned base URL: chat-completions.js:1689 reads azure_base_url from the request body, so both legs are aimed at the peer by the DRIVER.
tier2.pinnedSource: src/endpoints/backends/chat-completions.js:1700 new URL(`/openai/deployments/${azure_deployment_name}/chat/completions`, azure_base_url) -- a leading-slash path replaces the base path entirely

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
